text:
Jonas Weber: looping in Applied ML perf/evals on the workload suite + stats questions. we’re trying to lock the traffic shapes this week + variance budget so we can start baseline runs.

Jonas Weber: main questions:
1) representativeness: are we missing any common customer patterns (esp. long-context + streaming)?
2) methodology: trials / CI math / what we gate on (p95? p99? TTFT vs TPOT) without chasing noise.

Marcus Reed: +1. we have a draft set of shapes (short chat, long chat, embeddings, bursty concurrency, mixed prompt lengths) but need sign-off from ML side before we freeze v0.

Claire Dubois: thanks. i skimmed the draft. overall good, but i think the “long-context” shape is too clean right now.

Claire Dubois: most of the customer traces we’ve seen (even sanitized/aggregated) are bimodal: lots of 200-800 tok prompts and a smaller but meaningful tail at 8k-16k. if we only test 12k fixed, we’ll miss batching pathologies / scheduler interactions.

Rina Kobayashi: that’s doable. our generator can do mixture distributions. just need exact parameters.

Claire Dubois: proposal:
- prompt_len: mixture of (lognormal-ish short) + (uniform-ish long tail)
- output_len: separate distribution; long-context tends to have shorter outputs but not always
- concurrency: ramp + burst (so we see queue dynamics)

Arjun Desai: also worth splitting “long-context streaming” vs “long-context non-streaming”. streaming TTFT is usually fine; TPOT can get weird under contention.

Noah Patel: +1 from runtime side. baseline run 0 showed the only ugly outliers were long-context + streaming + bursty QPS.

Sana Farid: on methodology: please don’t gate on single-run p99 deltas for macro workloads. it’s the #1 way to create false alarms.

Sean Gallagher: (SRE) agree. we need something that’s stable enough to page on in nightly but not overly sensitive.

Sana Farid: what we’ve done in other perf suites:
- define a variance budget per metric per shape (p50, p95, p99, TTFT, TPOT, throughput)
- run N trials (e.g., 5-10) and compare distributions / bootstrap CI
- gate primarily on p95 (and TTFT p95) and use p99 as “investigate” unless it exceeds a larger threshold and is repeatable

Allison Grant: adding observability angle: p99 can be super sensitive to fleet mix + background jitter. if we use it, we need to annotate runs with hardware sku + driver/CUDA + host pool. otherwise it’s not actionable.

Marcus Reed: makes sense. how big should N be? we’re concerned about runtime/cost per nightly.

Sana Farid: depends on shape. for the “stable” shapes (non-streaming, moderate ctx), N=5 is usually sufficient. for bursty + tail-sensitive, N=10 if you want to say anything about p99.

Sana Farid: another option is to keep N=5 and focus the gate on p95 + TTFT p95 + throughput, and run a weekly “deep tail” job with N=20 for p99 characterization.

Sean Gallagher: that split would help. nightly shouldn’t take 6h.

Jonas Weber: can we put actual math/policy in the variance budget doc? i don’t want this living only in slack.

Sana Farid: yep. i can draft the section today.

Sana Farid: link (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/Benchmark+methodology+and+variance+budget

Noah Patel: re: what to gate on — i’d like to gate on TPOT for decode-heavy workloads too. we’ve had regressions where TTFT improved (prefill) but decode got slower.

Arjun Desai: agree, but define TPOT carefully for streaming. do we compute TPOT excluding first token (common) or inclusive? and do we use server timestamps only?

Allison Grant: we’ve been burned by client vs server clocks. please standardize on server-side timestamps for gating and keep client-measured as validation only.

Jonas Weber: yes, the telemetry validation work is already underway. gating should use runtime timestamps.

Claire Dubois: representativeness comment: we should include at least one “tool calling / structured output” shape. even if same token counts, it changes stop conditions and can affect decode patterns. could be modeled as higher stop-token frequency + shorter completions.

Rina Kobayashi: can simulate by setting tighter max_output and adding stop sequences. (we can keep prompts synthetic.)

Marcus Reed: does that belong in v0 or v1?

Claire Dubois: v0 if it’s cheap. otherwise v1.

Sana Farid: from a stats perspective, adding more shapes increases total comparisons => more false positives unless we’re careful. maybe keep v0 limited to a few high-impact shapes and add others after we stabilize variance budgets.

Sean Gallagher: +1. fewer shapes for gating, more shapes for reporting.

Jonas Weber: ok so suggestion:
- v0 gating shapes: short chat streaming, mixed prompt non-streaming, long-context streaming (mixture), embeddings batch
- v0 reporting-only shapes: tool-calling-ish, pure long ctx non-streaming, super-bursty tenant mix

Noah Patel: sounds good.

Arjun Desai: on metrics: for each shape, track:
- TTFT p50/p95
- TPOT p50/p95
- E2E latency p50/p95
- throughput (tok/s, req/s)
- error rate + timeouts

Arjun Desai: and please record token stats (actual prompt/out tokens). regressions sometimes are “workload drift” not runtime drift.

Rina Kobayashi: runner already emits prompt_tokens/output_tokens distribution summaries. can add to the output schema.

Sana Farid: statistical treatment suggestion (for doc):
- compute per-trial metric (e.g., p95 TTFT) for each trial
- compare candidate vs baseline using relative delta
- accept if delta within threshold OR if CI overlaps 0 within budget

Sana Farid: example language:
```
if (delta_p95_TTFT > 3%) and (bootstrap_95_CI_low > 0): regression
if (delta_p95_TTFT > 3%) and (bootstrap_95_CI crosses 0): warn-only
p99: investigate-only unless delta > 10% and reproduced in >=2 runs
```

Marcus Reed: super helpful.

Allison Grant: can we also add guidance on how to interpret deltas across HW? like H100 vs L40S, etc.

Arjun Desai: yes. normalization isn’t perfect, but we can at least avoid cross-SKU comparisons in gating. treat each (model, quant profile, hardware sku) as its own baseline.

Sean Gallagher: +1. gating across regions also: keep baselines per region group if fleet differs.

Jonas Weber: action items:
- Sana: add variance budget + CI guidance to the doc (and suggest nightly vs weekly run split)
- Claire: propose concrete mixture distribution params for long-context shape + whether tool-calling shape is v0
- Rina/Marcus: update workload generator + runner schema once params land

Sana Farid: ack. will post doc update in-thread.

Claire Dubois: i’ll send params by EOD. quick version now: 80% prompts ~ lognormal (median 500, sigma 0.8), 20% uniform [8k, 16k]. output: 70% uniform [64, 256], 30% uniform [256, 1024].

Noah Patel: perfect. that should trigger the batching / kv cache paths we care about.

Sean Gallagher: once doc is updated, please @ me on the regression thresholds section. SRE wants to align paging policy with it.

Jonas Weber: will do. thanks everyone.
